scoring_justification: Full recompute of the self-consistent solution would require reimplementing the nonlinear solver with all model parameters in the checker, which is not lightweight; comparing the agent's reported constants to paper gold with tolerances is the feasible verification method.

hidden_assets.purpose: Reference gold values for the self-consistent solution (delta, c, theta_C) taken from the paper.
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Paper: Metal-Semiconductor Transitions Induced by Adsorption of Alkali Metals on the Si(001) Surface, Davydov 2000. Section 3 reports delta=0.30 eV, c=0.32, and theta_C approx 0.4 for Cs/Si(001) under the assumptions V=D, epsilon_a^±=±delta, n_a=0.77, n_s=0.23.
hidden_assets.generation_method: Extracted directly from the paper text; the values are explicitly stated.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: The numbers are the paper's own reported results for the identical calculation the agent is asked to reproduce.

outputs.description: Self-consistently determined level splitting δ, charge-order parameter c, and critical coverage θ_C for Cs/Si(001) under the assumptions V=D, ε_a^±=±δ, n_a=0.77, n_s=0.23. Tolerances: δ ±0.05 eV, c ±0.05, θ_C ±0.1.

output_contract.notes: The verifier compares each value to paper-reported gold values with the listed tolerances. Full credit requires all three within tolerance; partial credit is proportional to the number of values passing.
